acceptance: A recorded analysis of the four breaches with the footprint inside and outside the holder tree.
A decided change, or a recorded decision to keep the behaviour, with the operator guidance in `docs/agent/heavy-work.md`.
context: Filed 2026-11-12 from the scale-factor follow-up and TPC-DI generator work of 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12: identified during that work and not addressed.
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12 four `make heavy-run HEAVY_ADMIT_WAIT=...` jobs from one session were admitted after waiting and then stopped by the watchdog with `BREACH memory pressure: measured level 4`, within about 15 s to 3 minutes of starting. The watchdog's own report showed the holder tree was small (ten dbgen processes at 0.29 GiB each in one case; a single Python generator in another). The pressure came from other sessions on a 16 GiB host with swap 90% to 95% used. Admission (pressure level 1 for a few samples) and the kill rule (level 4 at any moment) are far enough apart that a job can be admitted into a host that is about to breach, and the kill is not attributed: a light job dies for another process's memory. A 13-minute wait ended in a kill with no result, twice.

## Change
Options: require the admission condition to hold for longer before starting; make the kill decision consider the holder tree's share of the footprint, or pause instead of kill when the tree is small; report on a breach which processes outside the tree hold the memory; give `heavy-run` a retry-after-breach mode for idempotent commands.

## Guardrails
- The watchdog exists to stop the host from locking up; do not weaken the kill for a tree that is the cause.
- Never stop processes that belong to other sessions.
- Related: `heavy-guard-watchdog-20261030-deferral-1`.
